newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares gain 1.87 pct to new record.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares gain 1.87 pct to new record.

text.p: Istanbul shares maintained their strong uptrend on Wednesday with the index hitting another record although a ruling by the constitutional court on a law enabling Turk Telekom's privatisation was awaited, brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 closed at this year's 14th all-time high of 1,251, up 23 points, or 1.87 percent from Tuesday's previous record of 1,228. In dollar terms, it firmed to a new record of 1.09 cents from Tuesday's 1.08 cents.
Trade volume jumped to 29.40 trillion lira ($255.6 million) from Tuesday's 23.07 trillion ($202.1 million).
Brokers said falling money and bond market rates and quiet currency trade continued to divert money to shares.

Bond yields dived by as much as five points on Tuesday when the Treasury issued 399-day bonds at sharply lower rates in an auction. The central bank on Wednesday cut its money bid and offer rates by two and three points on lower bond yields.

"The market continued its rise while waiting for the constitutional court ruling on Telekom. Buying in shares of largely state-owned firms was the main factor that pulled the index up," said Yalcin Arican from Hak securities.
"I do not expect a major fall even if the court cancels the Telekom law because alternative markets are supporting the stock market's uptrend," he said.
The court debated for a second day the law designed for the sell-off of a partial stake in Telekom and the sale of GSM licences to private firms. The meeting will resume on Thursday.
The market index has surged 28.2 percent, breaking 14 record closes since the beginning of 1997. In dollar terms, it jumped 18.7 percent so far this year.
